# traceburn

> Finds and cuts wasted LLM spend. A local-first tracer for AI agents built on the
> openai and anthropic Python SDKs and litellm: a waste report that quantifies
> avoidable spend in dollars, a fix command that renders mechanical patches for two
> of the five waste patterns, a CI cost-regression gate, a cost and latency
> flamegraph, deterministic replay, and run diffs. One SQLite file, no account, no
> server, no telemetry.

Install: `pip install traceburn` (core, zero dependencies) or
`pip install "traceburn[ui]"` (adds the local web viewer). Requires Python 3.10+.

Patch an agent with two lines:

```python
import traceburn
traceburn.install()
```

Then: `traceburn waste <trace_id>` for the waste report, `traceburn fix <trace_id>`
for a literal patch where one is derivable, `traceburn check` as a CI threshold
gate, `traceburn ui` for the web viewer, `traceburn diff <a> <b>` to compare two
runs.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/TommyTranX/traceburn/blob/main/README.md): full
  pitch, install, quickstart, command reference, privacy and limitations.
- [docs/quickstart.md](https://github.com/TommyTranX/traceburn/blob/main/docs/quickstart.md):
  step-by-step first run.
- [docs/waste-rules.md](https://github.com/TommyTranX/traceburn/blob/main/docs/waste-rules.md):
  what each of the five waste rules detects and how the numbers are computed.
- [docs/fix-and-check.md](https://github.com/TommyTranX/traceburn/blob/main/docs/fix-and-check.md):
  the `fix` and `check` commands in detail, including the CI usage pattern.
- [docs/instrumentation.md](https://github.com/TommyTranX/traceburn/blob/main/docs/instrumentation.md):
  how the openai/anthropic/litellm patching works, and how to add a new adapter.
- [docs/replay.md](https://github.com/TommyTranX/traceburn/blob/main/docs/replay.md):
  deterministic, token-free replay of recorded calls.
- [docs/concepts.md](https://github.com/TommyTranX/traceburn/blob/main/docs/concepts.md):
  traces, spans, and sessions, and how they nest.

## Notes for agents

The CLI is scriptable and side-effect free except for `traceburn ui` (starts a
local server) and the initial `traceburn.install()` patch (in-process only,
no network calls of its own). `traceburn check` is meant to run in CI right
after a test suite records a trace, and exits nonzero on a threshold breach,
so it composes with any agent that already shells out to run tests.
